questions.column: How would you rate your repository’s technical readiness for integrating full digital traceability? Please choose what corresponds the most to your current situation. By “digital traceability,” we mean the structured, automated, and system-supported capture and linkage of associated data (e.g. preanalytical, clinical, research-derived), enabling traceability of a sample across its full lifecycle, from collection through processing, storage, use, and data generation. This includes the use of dedicated software (e.g. BIMS/LIMS), digital metadata standards, audit trails, and secure linkage to clinical data or research data.
questions.label: How would you rate your repository’s technical readiness for integrating full digital traceability? Please choose what corresponds the most to your current situation. By “digital traceability,” we mean the structured, automated, and system-supported capture and linkage of associated data (e.g. preanalytical, clinical, research-derived), enabling traceability of a sample across its full lifecycle, from collection through processing, storage, use, and data generation. This includes the use of dedicated software (e.g. BIMS/LIMS), digital metadata standards, audit trails, and secure linkage to clinical data or research data.
categories: Not started or fully manual: No digital traceability systems in place; tracking and data linkage are done manually or not at all.
Basic digital tools in use: Processes rely on spreadsheets or limited tools; traceability is possible but unstructured or inconsistent.
Partially digital, some key limitations: A digital system is in place (e.g., LIMS or custom DB), but linkage across data types is incomplete or metadata is not standardized.
Mostly digital with minor gaps: Most traceability processes are digital; structured data is used for key steps, and linkage to clinical/research data is possible with little effort.

Fully digital and interoperable: All associated data are managed through integrated, structured systems (e.g. BIMS), with routine linkage to clinical and research data; metadata standards (e.g. SPREC, MIABIS) and data protection compliant workflows are in place.
